summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy, was admitted with severe left lower quadrant abdominal pain, diarrhea up to 20 times daily with blood on wiping, and low-grade fevers. He was found to be dehydrated with acute kidney injury, likely pre-renal in etiology, and was treated with aggressive IV hydration, which resolved the renal dysfunction within 48 hours. A CT scan showed no obstruction or abscess, supporting a diagnosis of an acute Crohn’s flare. He was started on IV methylprednisolone and managed with IV then oral pain medications, including a short course of morphine. His anxiety, exacerbated by running out of quetiapine, improved with medication restart. Hypercalcemia noted on admission resolved spontaneously, with low PTH and low vitamin D levels suggesting a non-parathyroid cause. He progressed to a full diet, pain became well-controlled, and he was discharged home on a tapering course of prednisone, oral morphine for breakthrough pain, and continued pantoprazole and quetiapine, with strong advice to quit smoking.
